assumptions: Conversion is complete: every unmethylated C reads as T.
BSP avoids CpGs so it amplifies either state; MSP sits on them so it discriminates.
limits: The island scan is graded against EMBOSS cpgplot; the primer design has no runnable oracle (MethPrimer is web-only), so every returned pair is re-checked against the published rules by independent recomputation.
Incomplete conversion is a bench failure mode the design cannot see.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which BSP or MSP primers work on the bisulfite-converted strands, and where are the CpG islands?

description: Design BSP or MSP primers for a methylation assay, on the CONVERTED strands: after bisulfite treatment every unmethylated C reads as T, which is a different template from the one every other designer sees. BSP primers avoid CpGs so they amplify regardless of methylation state; MSP primers sit ON CpGs so they discriminate. Also reports the CpG islands (EMBOSS cpgplot) the assay should target.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

assay.description: BSP = bisulfite sequencing PCR: primers avoid CpG sites so both methylated and unmethylated template amplify equally, and the methylation is read from the SEQUENCE afterwards. MSP = methylation-specific PCR: primers cover CpG sites so amplification ITSELF is the readout. They answer different questions and are not interchangeable. Values: BSP (BSP - amplify regardless of methylation), MSP (MSP - amplify only one state).

criteria.description: which published criteria call a CpG island: Gardiner-Garden & Frommer 1987 as EMBOSS cpgplot encodes it, or the stricter Takai & Jones 2002, which excludes most Alu repeats. Values: cpgplot (Gardiner-Garden & Frommer (cpgplot)), takaiJones (Takai & Jones 2002 (promoter islands)).

design_in_island.description: design inside this island only, by its rank in the reported list (1 = first). Unset designs anywhere in the region; the panel instead asks for an island to be picked.

island_min_length.description: minimum island length (cpgplot -minlen); unset takes the preset's. In bp. Advanced.

island_min_obs_exp.description: minimum observed/expected CpG (cpgplot -minoe); unset takes the preset's. Advanced.

island_min_percent.description: minimum %C+%G (cpgplot -minpc); unset takes the preset's. In %. Advanced.

island_window.description: sliding window over which C, G and CpG are counted (cpgplot -window); unset takes the preset's. In bp. Advanced.

max_cpg_distance_from_3.description: MSP ONLY. How close to the 3' end the last CpG must sit. A mismatch discriminates most strongly at the 3' end, because that is where the polymerase extends. In nt. Advanced.

max_length.description: longest primer considered. In nt. Advanced.

max_results.description: how many primer pairs to return, best first.

max_tm.description: primers above this Tm are rejected outright. In °C. Advanced.

min_cpg.description: MSP ONLY. The fewest CpG sites a primer must cover, so it can discriminate methylated from unmethylated at all. In sites.

min_gc.description: lowest acceptable GC. The floor is low on purpose: after conversion every unmethylated C is a T, so converted DNA is genuinely GC-poor and an ordinary 40% floor rejects correct primers. In %. Advanced.

min_length.description: shortest primer considered. In nt. Advanced.

min_non_cpg_c.description: BSP ONLY. The fewest non-CpG cytosines the ORIGINAL sequence under a primer must carry - the rule that makes a BSP primer bisulfite-SPECIFIC, because those cytosines become T only if conversion worked. A primer with none anneals to untreated DNA just as well and the assay silently reports on template that was never converted. In nt.

min_tm.description: primers below this Tm are rejected outright. In °C. Advanced.

opt_length.description: primer length the ranking prefers. In nt.

opt_tm.description: target Tm; candidates rank by distance from it. Bisulfite-converted DNA is C-poor, so these run lower than an ordinary design. In °C.

region_end.description: 0-based inclusive end. Unset = the whole sequence. Advanced.

region_start.description: 0-based inclusive start of the region to design in. Unset = the whole sequence; pass the selection's start to scope to it. Advanced.

name: design_bisulfite_primers

assay.description: which assay was designed, echoed so a result never has to be guessed at

forward.description: the best pair's forward primer (wire into pcr_amplify)

islandCount.description: how many CpG islands were found

islands.description: CpG islands in the record (EMBOSS cpgplot criteria) - what a methylation assay should be aimed at

methylatedPairs.description: MSP: the pairs specific for the METHYLATED allele. Empty under BSP

pairs.description: the primer pairs, best first: each with both oligos, their coordinates on the ORIGINAL unconverted sequence, Tm, GC, CpG count and the non-CpG C conversion check

unmethylatedPairs.description: MSP: the pairs specific for the UNMETHYLATED allele - the other half of the assay, and the control that tells a negative from a failed reaction. Empty under BSP
